intro.heading: Restore Your Health with Oral Surgery in Santa Clarita
paragraphs: Oral surgery doesn’t have to be overwhelming—at Valencia Dentistry, we make it a comfortable, empowering experience. Whether you need a wisdom tooth removed, bone grafting for dental implants, or treatment for chronic infection, our oral surgery in Santa Clarita is designed with your comfort and results in mind. Your dentist and our experienced team combine advanced technology, gentle techniques, and personalized care to help you heal faster and feel better. From consultation to recovery, we’re here to guide you every step of the way.

process.heading: Our Oral Surgery Process: What to Expect
process.intro: At Valencia Dentistry, we take the stress out of oral surgery with a step-by-step approach that’s clear, comfortable, and fully personalized. From your initial consultation to post-op recovery, our team is here to guide you through every phase with compassion and transparency.

steps.title: Consultation & Digital Imaging
steps.text: We begin with a comprehensive exam, 3D imaging, and a detailed discussion of your symptoms and goals. Your dentist will walk you through your options and design a surgical plan that fits your unique needs.

steps.title: Surgery Day
steps.text: Your procedure is performed in-office using local anesthesia and optional sedation. Whether you’re having a tooth removed or receiving implants, we use precise techniques and advanced tools to ensure optimal results with minimal discomfort.

steps.title: Recovery & Follow-Up
steps.text: After surgery, we provide detailed instructions and schedule follow-up visits to monitor healing. Most patients recover quickly and return to normal activities within a few days, depending on the procedure performed.

candidate.heading: Are you a good candidate for oral surgery?

care.heading: Pre- and Post-Op Care for Oral Surgery
before: Follow fasting instructions if sedation is planned
Pause certain medications only if advised by your dentist
Arrange for someone to drive you home if sedation will be used
Avoid smoking and alcohol for at least 24 hours prior
Maintain good oral hygiene to reduce infection risk
after: Rest and limit physical activity for the first 24–48 hours
Eat soft, cool foods like yogurt, smoothies, and soup
Avoid drinking through a straw, smoking, or spitting forcefully
Use ice packs and prescribed medications to manage swelling and discomfort
Keep the surgical area clean with gentle brushing and saltwater rinses

faqs.a: Most oral surgeries are performed under local anesthesia, and we offer sedation options for added comfort. You may experience mild soreness afterward, but most patients report less discomfort than expected.

faqs.q: How long is recovery after oral surgery?
faqs.a: Initial recovery usually takes 2–5 days, depending on the procedure. Complete healing—especially for implants or bone grafts—can take several weeks to a few months.

faqs.q: What can I eat after oral surgery?
faqs.a: Stick to soft foods like smoothies, mashed potatoes, yogurt, soup, and scrambled eggs for the first few days. Avoid crunchy, spicy, or hot foods until cleared by our team.

faqs.q: How much does oral surgery cost?
faqs.a: Costs vary by procedure and insurance coverage. We provide transparent pricing and offer financing options to make treatment accessible.

faqs.q: Do you offer sedation for anxious patients?
faqs.a: Yes. We offer nitrous oxide and oral sedation to help you stay calm and comfortable throughout your procedure.

faqs.q: When should wisdom teeth be removed?
faqs.a: Wisdom teeth are often removed between ages 17–25, especially if they’re impacted, misaligned, or causing pain. Early removal can help prevent future complications.

faqs.q: How do I know if I need oral surgery?
faqs.a: If you’re dealing with persistent tooth pain, swelling, jaw discomfort, or preparing for implants, oral surgery might be necessary. Learn more about common surgical dental procedures and when they’re recommended from this Mayo Clinic overview on oral surgery.

faqs.q: Can I get oral surgery if I have a medical condition?
faqs.a: Many patients with medical conditions can safely undergo oral surgery. Your dentist will review your full health history to ensure any necessary precautions are taken.
